name: Nitti OAB Trial
question: Does intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA 100 U reduce urinary incontinence and improve patient-rated treatment benefit over placebo in overactive bladder inadequately managed with anticholinergics?

design.population: Adults with idiopathic overactive bladder, at least 3 urgency incontinence episodes in 3 days and at least 8 micturitions a day, inadequately managed with anticholinergics.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 randomized trial
design.locator: Abstract; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00910845 participant flow and eligibility; FDA label (2013) p20, section 14.1

verdictNote: Both coprimary endpoints improved at week 12; urinary tract infection and retention were more frequent.
takeaway: In overactive bladder with urgency incontinence inadequately managed by anticholinergics, intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA 100 U reduced daily incontinence episodes more than placebo at week 12 (−2.65 versus −0.87) and produced more positive treatment benefit responses (60.8% versus 29.2%); retention within 12 weeks was 5.4%.

reports.label: Phase 3 randomized report
reports.citation: Nitti VW, Dmochowski R, Herschorn S, et al. "OnabotulinumtoxinA for the Treatment of Patients with Overactive Bladder and Urinary Incontinence: Results of a Phase 3, Randomized, Placebo Controlled Trial." *J Urol.* 2013;189(6):2186-2193. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2012.12.022
reports.followUp: Week 12 primary endpoints within a 24-week placebo-controlled cycle

results.measure: Mean change from baseline in daily urinary incontinence episodes at week 12 (coprimary); difference is the ANCOVA least-squares mean difference, onabotulinumtoxinA minus placebo
results.note: Mean changes from baselines of 5.47 and 5.09 episodes per day (n = 280 and 277; SD of change 3.33 and 2.83). The difference and interval are from the FDA label's Study OAB-1 table (least-squares mean change −2.5 versus −0.9; n = 278 and 272; ANCOVA with last observation carried forward).
results.locator: Abstract; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00910845 outcome measures; FDA label (2013) p20, Table 16

results.measure: Proportion with a positive response on the treatment benefit scale at week 12 (coprimary)
Mean change from baseline in daily micturition episodes at week 12; least-squares mean change and difference, onabotulinumtoxinA minus placebo
results.note: Baselines 12.0 and 11.2 micturitions per day. Unadjusted mean changes were −2.15 and −0.91 (n = 280 and 277).
results.locator: FDA label (2013) p20, Table 16; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00910845 outcome measures

results.measure: Mean change from baseline in volume voided per micturition (mL) at week 12; least-squares mean change and difference, onabotulinumtoxinA minus placebo
results.note: Baselines 156 and 161 mL. Unadjusted mean changes were +41.1 and +9.7 mL (n = 280 and 277).
results.locator: FDA label (2013) p20, Table 16; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00910845 outcome measures

results.measure: All other overactive bladder symptoms, week 12 versus placebo
Health-related quality of life across multiple measures, week 12
Median duration of response by qualification for retreatment (pooled Study OAB-1 and OAB-2)
results.note: Pooled across this trial and its companion trial, so not specific to this trial. The label gives a range across the two studies for 100 U and one figure for placebo.

harms.label: Urinary tract infection
harms.locator: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00910845 adverse events (placebo-controlled cycle 1, safety population)
harms.note: The abstract reports uncomplicated urinary tract infection as the most common adverse event.

harms.label: Urinary retention
harms.locator: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00910845 adverse events (placebo-controlled cycle 1, safety population); abstract
harms.note: The abstract gives a urinary retention rate of 5.4% (15 of 278) within the first 12 weeks; the registry counts 16 of 278 treated patients at any time in cycle 1.

harms.label: Dysuria
harms.locator: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00910845 adverse events (placebo-controlled cycle 1, safety population)

harms.label: Bacteriuria
harms.locator: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00910845 adverse events (placebo-controlled cycle 1, safety population)

harms.label: Hematuria
harms.locator: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00910845 adverse events (placebo-controlled cycle 1, safety population)
harms.note: Listed in the registry because it reached 5% in the placebo group.

harms.label: Serious adverse events (any cause)
harms.locator: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00910845 adverse events (placebo-controlled cycle 1, safety population)
harms.note: Pneumonia and depression were the only serious event terms reported in two onabotulinumtoxinA patients; every other term was reported in one.

harms.label: Urinary tract infection within 12 weeks (pooled Study OAB-1 and OAB-2)
harms.note: Pooled across this trial and its companion trial.

harms.label: Clean intermittent catheterization for urinary retention (pooled Study OAB-1 and OAB-2)
harms.note: At any time during the treatment cycle. Median duration of catheterization was 63 days (range 1 to 214) after onabotulinumtoxinA and 11 days (range 3 to 18) after placebo.

harms.label: Urinary retention by history of diabetes (pooled Study OAB-1 and OAB-2)
harms.note: Pooled across this trial and its companion trial.

harms.label: Urinary tract infection by history of diabetes (pooled Study OAB-1 and OAB-2)
harms.note: Among onabotulinumtoxinA recipients, urinary tract infection occurred in 44% of those with a maximum post-injection post-void residual above 200 mL and 23% of those below 200 mL.

delivery.label: Registry eligibility
delivery.value: Age 18 years or older; overactive bladder with incontinence for at least 6 months; randomized 1:1
delivery.note: Excluded: overactive bladder from a neurologic condition, stress-predominant incontinence, and any history or evidence of pelvic or urologic abnormality.

delivery.label: Age 65 years or older
delivery.note: Sum of the 65 to 74 and 75 or older age bands; 90 patients were 75 or older (46 and 44).

delivery.label: Study treatment
delivery.value: 20 intradetrusor injections of 5 U (onabotulinumtoxinA or placebo), about 1 cm apart; 100 U total
delivery.note: The label describes this pattern for both pivotal OAB studies.

delivery.label: Injection plane
delivery.value: Trigone-sparing injection in the placebo-controlled trials in the AUA/SUFU evidence base
delivery.locator: AUA/SUFU OAB guideline 2024, p33 (cites this trial among references 236 and 238 to 240)
delivery.note: The statement covers the group of trials, not this trial alone.

delivery.label: Entered treatment cycle 2
delivery.note: A repeat injection of 100 U after at least 12 weeks, where applicable; placebo recipients received onabotulinumtoxinA 100 U in cycle 2.

delivery.label: Retreatment criteria
delivery.value: At least 12 weeks since the prior injection, post-void residual below 200 mL and at least 2 incontinence episodes over 3 days
delivery.note: Median time to qualify for the second treatment was 169 days (about 24 weeks) in the two placebo-controlled studies (p5).

delivery.label: Labeled injection technique (OAB dose)
delivery.value: 100 U in 10 mL nonpreserved saline through a flexible or rigid cystoscope, trigone avoided, bladder not overdistended, needle about 2 mm into the detrusor, 20 injections of 0.5 mL about 1 cm apart; patient observed at least 30 minutes and until a spontaneous void
delivery.note: Label instructions, not the trial protocol.

delivery.label: Labeled pre- and post-procedure measures
delivery.value: No urinary tract infection at treatment; antibiotic prophylaxis (not aminoglycosides) 1 to 3 days before, on the day and 1 to 3 days after; antiplatelet therapy stopped at least 3 days before
delivery.note: Label instructions, not the trial protocol.

reports.label: 3.5-year extension
reports.citation: Nitti VW, Ginsberg D, Sievert KD, et al. "Durable Efficacy and Safety of Long-Term OnabotulinumtoxinA Treatment in Patients with Overactive Bladder Syndrome: Final Results of a 3.5-Year Study." *J Urol.* 2016;196(3):791-800. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2016.03.146
reports.followUp: Up to 3.5 years: 3-year extension after the 24-week phase 3 trials, up to 6 as-needed treatments

results.measure: Mean change from baseline in daily incontinence episodes at week 12 after each treatment, overall population (range across up to 6 treatments)
results.note: Open-label extension of patients who completed either phase 3 trial; no control group. Discrete subgroups receiving 1 to 6 treatments ranged from −2.9 to −4.5.

harms.label: De novo intermittent catheterization

values.exp: 4.0% after the first treatment; 0.6% to 1.7% after subsequent treatments

harms.note: Urinary tract infection was the most common adverse event.

delivery.label: Extension regimen
delivery.value: OnabotulinumtoxinA as needed; outcomes reported for 100 U treatments 1 to 6
delivery.note: Patients who completed either of the two 24-week phase 3 trials could enter a 3-year extension.

relations.note: Same drug and sponsor, placebo-controlled phase 3 design; Ginsberg studied neurogenic detrusor overactivity at higher doses, this trial idiopathic OAB at 100 U.
